about: The Social Security Fairness Act: the end of the two reductions for people with a pension from work not covered by Social Security.

rows.plain: The Social Security Fairness Act, signed on January 5, 2025, ended the Windfall Elimination Provision and the Government Pension Offset.
It applies to benefits for January 2024 and later. December 2023 was the last month either reduction applied.
Social Security began adjusting monthly payments on February 25, 2025. Most affected people began getting the new monthly amount in April 2025.
Back pay is a one-time payment for the increase back to January 2024, sent to the bank account Social Security has on file.
Affected people get a mailed notice, sometimes two. The back pay may arrive before the notice.
People who never applied because of these reductions may need to file an application. The date you apply can affect when benefits start and how much they are.
Retirement or spouse's benefits can be applied for online or by phone. Survivors benefits cannot be applied for online.
For retirement and survivors benefits, a new application generally reaches back no more than six months before the month you apply. The Act did not change that rule.
Check that your mailing address and direct deposit details are right in your my Social Security account, or by phone if you cannot open one.
Once benefits start, Social Security takes the Medicare premium out of the monthly payment. If you pay Medicare directly, keep paying the bill until Social Security writes to you.
Social Security will never ask for payment to start, increase or speed up benefits.
Social Security: 1-800-772-1213, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. local time.
